notes: SIGKILL mid-turn, single top-level session -- mirrors claudecode's own 2-25 phase shape (session_birth/pid_bind/turn_start/process_exit, invariant 'no state_transition to error') but with a widened process_exit window versus claudecode's 20000ms, for the same reason: this scenario's own description states its daemon-side outcome is identical to muse's 1-2_session-end variant 3 (SIGKILL mid-turn), which this branch already recorded live (recordings/2026-09-14-05-59-39_irrlichd-0.6.3+e22b8c9/) and whose meta notes document a real, twice-reproduced race against #1962 (processlifecycle's kqueue watched map[int]string last-write-wins): every muse session launch also spawns a transient proc-<pid> presession watching the SAME OS pid, so the fast kqueue NOTE_EXIT callback can misattribute this session's own exit to that shadow instead. The redundant PIDManager.CheckPIDLiveness -> reapDeadOrInfraPID sweep (pid_manager.go:1095/1186, syscall.Kill probe keyed on each session's OWN persisted PID field, never on the shared kqueue map) recovers the correct session's process_exited within one sweep tick (5s base / 15s worst-case backoff) regardless of which path the fast kqueue callback took. process_exit is pinned with same_session_as to the real session specifically so an unpinned search cannot vacuously pass by matching the shadow's own (differently-timed) exit instead -- the same fix 1-2_session-end's spec needed after a live run proved the unpinned form matches the wrong session. Session-birth/pid-bind/process-exit timing bounds are carried over from claudecode's proven template and muse's own 1-2_session-end recording; record should tighten them once this specific cell has its own live capture. PRE-DRIVE SPEC FIX (#1960 record pass): pid_bind was originally relative_to "start" with no same_session_as, unpinned. This batch's own two prior cells (2-9, 2-22 recordings, same session) directly observed a genuine ~100-150ms race between the real session and its own transient proc-<PID> presession for who reaches 'ready'/gets pid_discovered first -- an unpinned phase can silently bind to the presession instead of the real session. Retargeted to relative_to session_birth + same_session_as session_birth, matching every other muse cell's pattern (2-14/2-22/2-23/2-9), before this cell's own first live drive rather than discovering it the hard way. LIVE RESULT (2026-09-14, promoted recording 2026-09-14-22-49-23_irrlichd-0.6.3+fa2b2c3): 4/4 phases passed, including the 'no state_transition to error' invariant. The recipe's own sigkill/lsof write-mode filter worked exactly as designed (the coexisting recording daemon holds a read fd on the same .session.lock; the filter correctly resolved the real muse-bin writer PID and never touched the daemon). #1962 did NOT reproduce on the promoted attempt: process_exited landed directly on the real session via the fast kqueue path (~4.07s after turn_start), not its proc-<PID> shadow -- so max_delay_ms=20000 had ample margin without needing the periodic sweep. The completeness checker flagged this recording 'suspect: unsettled' (last state_transition was 'working', no further transition before the recording ends) -- this is the CORRECT, expected shape for this scenario (the row is deleted via process_exited, never settled to another state), waived per the skill's documented pattern via a per-staging completeness-waiver.json rather than editing the shared scenarios.json catalog (a one-off, not a repo-wide declaration this assessment pass is positioned to make). CONFIRMED HAZARD, cited per the batch brief: a FIRST live attempt (discarded, not promoted) hit a REAL transient 429 rate_limited response from the genuine Meta backend (request_id 89709bca-7c31-4758-8170-e1192a86a58f, http_status 429, error_kind rate_limited, ~1.3s real round-trip) -- unrelated to the SIGKILL, occurring ~40 microseconds after turn_start in daemon-observed time, painting the session 'error' via the SAME session_error/retrying mechanism 2-9/2-22/2-23 use, well before the kill landed. This recipe carries no --base-url override (unlike the mock-driven siblings), so it talks to the REAL account; at the time, two OTHER long-running muse-bin processes (unrelated ttys, started independently of this task) were confirmed active on this machine (ps aux), which is the most likely source of the ambient real-account rate pressure, not this recipe's own actions. Per the 'never induce a real quota exhaustion' rule, this was treated as a single, low-risk retry (an ordinary self-healing 429, not an exhaustion) rather than repeated hammering; the discarded attempt's own state arc (working->error at t+~1.3s, never killed cleanly mid-working) was NOT promoted because it does not represent this scenario's intended elicitation (a session that is genuinely still 'working', not already 'error' for an unrelated reason, at kill time) -- captured here as a documented caveat instead, per this batch's own instruction to confirm the session was still working when the kill fired.
